messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the gateway fanout change in ap-southeast we flipped yesterday, Grafana is showing a jump in tail latency and ~25-30% of traces are missing runtime spans (worker/*). Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:
jihoon: saw a handful of those traces in the tracing UI this morning. spans are there at the ingress but vanish before the runtime service. suspect propagation/header stripping at the new edge pool.
sam: ops-bot alert kicked off: `ALERT TracingHighTailLatency` fired in the last 30m, and cost ingestion is up from tail-sampling changes. linking dashboard: https://grafana/internal/d/reds/traces-slo
leo: can you paste an example trace id? also which gateway rollout PR was that?
maya: example trace id: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01. in spans you see ingress and then nothing. rollout PR is #4253 — changed fanout to 8 and enabled connection multiplexing in edge-proxy.
jihoon: edge-proxy config might be rewriting incoming headers. our OTEL header is `traceparent` + `tracestate`. proxy default removes unknown headers unless allowlist configured.
sam: ops-bot: show last deploy for edge-proxy in ap-southeast
ops-bot: deploy edge-proxy ap-southeast v3.12.0 started by @maya at 2026-02-28T21:34:00Z, completed 2026-02-28T21:42:10Z.
leo: quick check — in the collector logs I can see the otel-collector in ap-southeast receiving spans with empty parent_id for many traces. snippet from collector.log:
```
2026-02-28T21:45:12Z INFO received span id=00f067aa0ba902b7 parent_id="" trace_id=4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 service=ingress
```
seems parent header got dropped.
maya: sounds like header allowlist issue. we added the new edge pool under a different ingress role; allowlist config didn't include `traceparent`.
jihoon: agree. short fix: update edge-proxy config to forward `traceparent` and `tracestate` and restart only the ap-southeast pool. patch ready: `proxy.conf: headers_forward: [traceparent, tracestate, x-cloud-trace-context]`.
sam: before we roll, note cost: fixing this will increase trace ingestion because our tail sampler currently ramps up on partial traces — we had tail-sampling tuned to drop ~60% in apac to reduce cost. If we suddenly start receiving full context we might ingest 2-3x more spans. ops, are we ok with that?
leo: we should estimate impact. quick query from prometheus: `sum(rate(otel_spans_received_total{region="ap-southeast"}[5m]))` shows ~1.2k/s now; if we restore propagation upstream it could go to ~3k/s based on prior peaks.
maya: short term I want the propagation fixed (visibility > cost). But let's gate with a temporary sampling cap on the collector. Proposal: forward headers, add `processing: tail_sampling: max_spans_per_minute: 150000` to keep ingestion under control while we observe.
jihoon: can do. also recommend we add a small rewrite in proxy to copy `x-request-id` -> `traceparent` for any legacy clients that dropped it, and add logs when `traceparent` missing to monitor fix rate.
sam: I'll update billing alarm thresholds and capacity alerts. Also add a Grafana panel showing `percent_traces_with_missing_runtime_spans` (heuristic: traces where ingress exists but runtime span count is 0) so we can track rollout impact.
leo: will open canary rollback playbook if error budget blowups. suggest we set an alert: `SLO: trace_visibility_drop` if >15% of traces missing runtime spans for 10m.
maya: thank you. plan: (1) roll edge-proxy header allowlist to include tracing headers in ap-southeast (canary 10%), (2) add collector tail_sampling cap, (3) monitor Grafana panel and alerts for 30m, (4) if ingestion delta >2x revert fanout. I'll post PRs and timestamps here.
jihoon: FYI I found a small proxy bug where connection multiplexing strips headers when `preserve_headers: false` — setting it true fixes without full restart. patching now.
sam: noted. I'll lower the billing alert threshold by 20% while we monitor.
ops-bot: alert update: TracingHighTailLatency -> acknowledged by @maya.
maya: rolling canary now (ap-southeast-1a), ETA 5m. will update when complete. :thumbsup:
